speed-lanes.prompt: Under California's Basic Speed Law, you may never drive:

options.text: Faster than the posted limit, even in an emergency
Slower than the flow of traffic
Faster than is safe for current conditions
Faster than 55 mph on any two-lane road

speed-lanes.explanation: The basic speed law requires driving no faster than is safe for weather, traffic, and road conditions, regardless of the posted limit.

speed-lanes.prompt: Unless otherwise posted, the speed limit on a two-lane undivided highway in California is:
speed-lanes.explanation: Two-lane undivided highways are limited to 55 mph unless signs show a different limit.

speed-lanes.prompt: You are on a freeway posted 65 mph in clear weather with light traffic. You may legally drive:

options.text: 70 mph to keep up with faster traffic
As fast as the flow of traffic

speed-lanes.explanation: The posted limit is the maximum even when passing or keeping up with traffic; most California freeways are limited to 65 mph unless posted 70.

speed-lanes.prompt: What is the speed limit in an alley in California?
speed-lanes.explanation: The limit in any alley is 15 mph, the same limit used at blind intersections and blind railroad crossings.

speed-lanes.prompt: When children are outside or crossing near a school, the speed limit is usually:

options.text: 25 mph unless a lower limit is posted

speed-lanes.explanation: Within 500 to 1,000 feet of a school while children are outside, the limit is 25 mph unless posted lower.

speed-lanes.prompt: Which vehicles may use an HOV (carpool) lane during its restricted hours?

options.text: Any vehicle that is passing slower traffic
Vehicles with at least the posted number of occupants, motorcycles, and vehicles with an eligible decal
Any vehicle driving at or above the speed limit

speed-lanes.explanation: HOV lanes are for vehicles meeting the posted occupancy minimum, plus motorcycles and decal-eligible clean-air vehicles.

speed-lanes.prompt: If you drive slower than the flow of traffic on a multilane freeway, you should:

options.text: Turn on your hazard lights and use any lane
Use the left lane so others can pass on the right

speed-lanes.explanation: Slower traffic must keep right; the left lanes are for passing and faster-moving traffic.

speed-lanes.prompt: While another vehicle is passing you on the left, you should:

options.text: Speed up slightly so the pass is completed sooner
Move onto the shoulder to make room
Honk to warn the other driver
Maintain or slightly reduce your speed and stay in your lane

speed-lanes.explanation: Never speed up while being passed; hold or ease your speed so the other driver can return to the lane safely.

options.text: No stopping, standing, or parking at any time
Passenger pickup for up to 5 minutes

parking-stopping.explanation: Red curbs prohibit stopping, standing, or parking; buses may stop only at red zones marked for buses.

parking-stopping.prompt: You may stop at a white painted curb only:

options.text: Long enough to load or unload freight
If you leave your hazard lights on
Long enough to pick up or drop off passengers or mail

parking-stopping.explanation: White curbs allow only brief stops to pick up or drop off passengers or deposit mail.

parking-stopping.prompt: You may not park within what distance of a fire hydrant?
parking-stopping.explanation: California law prohibits parking within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.

parking-stopping.prompt: A curb painted blue means parking is allowed:

options.text: For anyone for up to 15 minutes
Only for disabled persons displaying a placard or special plates

parking-stopping.explanation: Blue curbs are reserved for drivers or passengers with a valid disabled placard or disabled license plates.

parking-stopping.prompt: When parking downhill next to a curb, you should turn your front wheels:

options.text: Straight ahead with the parking brake off
In either direction, as long as the parking brake is set

parking-stopping.explanation: Downhill, wheels turn into the curb so the car rolls against it if the brakes fail; uphill with a curb, turn them away.

options.text: Stop only long enough to load or unload passengers or freight, usually staying with your vehicle
No parking at any time for any reason
Free parking for the time posted on the curb

parking-stopping.explanation: Yellow zones are for loading and unloading; drivers of noncommercial vehicles are usually expected to stay with the vehicle.

parking-stopping.prompt: Under California law, how close to a crosswalk may you park?

options.text: Right up to the crosswalk if no sign prohibits it

parking-stopping.explanation: California's daylighting law prohibits parking within 20 feet of any marked or unmarked crosswalk to keep pedestrians visible.

options.text: Parking for a limited time shown on the curb or a nearby sign

parking-stopping.explanation: Green curbs allow parking only for the limited time painted on the curb or posted on a sign.

alcohol-penalties.prompt: For drivers 21 and older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:
alcohol-penalties.explanation: The legal limit for noncommercial drivers 21 and older is 0.08%; commercial drivers are limited to 0.04%.

alcohol-penalties.prompt: Under California's zero tolerance law, drivers under 21 may not drive with a BAC of:
alcohol-penalties.explanation: Drivers under 21 violate the zero tolerance law with a BAC of just 0.01% or higher.

alcohol-penalties.prompt: California's implied consent law means that by driving in the state you have agreed to:

options.text: Carry proof of insurance at all times
Attend DUI school if you are ever stopped
Let officers search your vehicle at any time
Submit to a chemical test of your blood or breath if lawfully arrested for DUI

alcohol-penalties.explanation: Holding a license and driving in California implies consent to BAC testing after a lawful DUI arrest.

alcohol-penalties.prompt: If you refuse to take a chemical test after a lawful DUI arrest:

options.text: The DUI charges must be dropped
Your license will be suspended, and you can still be convicted of DUI
You will only pay a small fine
You may substitute a field sobriety test instead

alcohol-penalties.explanation: Refusal triggers a license suspension on its own and does not prevent a DUI conviction.

alcohol-penalties.prompt: A driver under 21 caught driving with a BAC of 0.01% or higher will:

options.text: Have their driving privilege suspended for one year
Receive only a warning for a first offense
Pay a fine but keep their license if under 0.05%
Be required to retake the written knowledge test

alcohol-penalties.explanation: Under zero tolerance, a BAC of 0.01% or more results in a one-year suspension of an under-21 driver's license.

alcohol-penalties.prompt: An opened container of alcohol carried in a vehicle must be kept:

options.text: Under a seat, out of reach
In the back seat next to a sober passenger
In the trunk or another area where passengers do not sit

alcohol-penalties.explanation: Open containers must be in the trunk or a place not occupied by passengers; the glove box is specifically illegal.

alcohol-penalties.prompt: A DUI conviction stays on your California driving record for:
alcohol-penalties.explanation: A DUI remains on your DMV record for 10 years and counts as a prior offense during that period.

alcohol-penalties.prompt: How many points does a DUI conviction add to your California driving record?
alcohol-penalties.explanation: A DUI counts as a 2-point violation; 4 points in 12 months can classify you as a negligent operator.
